newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RBNZ to hold conditions at current levels - BTNZ.
newsitem.headline: RBNZ to hold conditions at current levels - BTNZ.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand will hold monetary conditions at current levels when it releases its next round of forecasts on September 13, Bankers Trust economists predicted on Tuesday.

BT said it expected the RBNZ would assume a policy mix of a New Zealand dollar Trade-Weighted Index of 65.5 for the December quarter, appreciating at 1.7 percent per annum, and a 90-day bank bill rate of around 10 percent over the course of the forecasts.
"This set of conditions will produce a very favourable medium term inflation outlook," the economists said in a commentary.
"The forecasts are likely to show inflation well below 1.0 percent by the end of 1997 and lower still in 1998."

BT said the RBNZ's medium term outlook should be favourable for the bond market. "While the market is already pricing in a sizeable easing, the even lower inflation outlook for late 1997 will support this and possibly lead to a greater easing being priced in."
BT said the main risk to its view was that the RBNZ could ease on September 13.

"The medium term inflation outlook would certainly justify such a move. A more moderate response could be for the RBNZ to signal that the tightening in conditions relative to the assumptions it made in June (bank bills at 10 percent and TWI and 64.0) is unnecessary," it said.
While the RBNZ may consider such a statement to be a "rebalancing" rather than an easing, the market would interpret it as an easing signal.
"The signalling difficulties associated with a move such as this make it unlikely," BT said.
"On balance, we think the RBNZ will not ease policy in September. Nor will it factor in an easing at a later date."

BT said a significant post-election easing in fiscal policy may remove much, if not all, of the room for monetary policy to ease. It also said it was not yet clear whether housing prices had begun to fall.
BT said most commentators were not looking for an easing until the end of 1996 at the earliest and a statement along these lines would be broadly in line with market expectations.
